description: Multilingual routing probes (routing-360 Phase 3.4) — 12 Latin-script briefs (es/fr/it/de) + 3 CJK smokes (zh/ja/ko), languages with zero corpus presence but clearly in-domain intent. accepted_targets lists every squad/business that legitimately owns the domain. This is the regime a dense multilingual arm was expected to win. MEASURED 2026-08-05 (neural backend Xenova/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 active, corpus 1508 docs): baseline (dense off) signals were 12x NO_MATCH + 3x AMBIGUOUS, zero HIGH. Dense top-1 cosines on the 12 NO_MATCH probes ranged 0.335-0.655 with the CORRECT target on top in 7/12 — but the out-of-domain negatives (golden-negatives.json) score 0.161-0.471 on the same index, so the bands OVERLAP: correct hits at 0.371/0.441/0.463 sit BELOW the negatives max (0.471, a dishwasher brief cosine-close to a kitchen-ops employee). At the safe threshold 0.55 (0.079 above the negatives max) the fallback recovers only 3/12 probes (2 with a correct suggestion; CJK 0/3). DECISION: the dense NO_MATCH fallback slot exists (router.js Stage 3.5, suggestion-only, AMBIGUOUS ceiling) but routing.dense defaults to "off"; `nrv embeddings enable` opts in. The CI test (routing-multilingual-probes.test.ts) pins the decided behavior: these briefs must NEVER dispatch HIGH, and with the default config no dense suggestion appears.
